title: dev.qory.run.egress
description: One connection the session requested through the proxy, with the decision, the rule that made it and what became of it. Every connection is one event, allowed or denied. To a host the proxy terminates TLS for, every request is one event instead, with its path; to a host a tool serves, every request is a tool invocation and contains the tool.

host.description: The host the session requested, as a lower-case name or an IP literal.

method.description: CONNECT for a tunnel, HTTP for a plain request through the proxy, HTTPS for a request inside a connection the proxy terminates.

request_method.description: The request's method, such as GET or POST, with HTTPS.

path.description: The request's path, without its query, with HTTPS.

path_rule.description: The path entry that matched, of the policy's or the credential's, when the host has path rules; empty when none did, which is denied under enforce. wall:ambiguous-path when the path could be read two ways, denied in either mode.

credential.description: The name of the credential the proxy set on the request, when it set one. Never its value.

tool.description: The name of the tool that serves the host, on a request the proxy decides by its path: passed to the tool when allowed, a tool invocation, and not when a path rule refuses it. A connection refused by its host has no tool.

request_id.description: The proxy's own id of a request it read, with HTTP and HTTPS: what a tool receives as the Qory-Request-Id header.

status.description: The status the host or the tool returned for the request, with HTTP and HTTPS, when one returned one: absent when the request was refused or not delivered.

outcome.description: What became of the connection. connected: the dial succeeded. dial_failed: allowed, and the dial failed. refused: not dialled, because the policy or the wall's guard denied it, or closed by the proxy when a new run configuration denied its host.

mode.description: The policy mode the decision was made under.

rule.description: The allow entry that matched the host, or empty when none did. In observe mode an empty rule is still allowed; in enforce mode it is denied. Behind a wall, wall:own-address is the wall's own refusal, in either mode: the host is a link-local address, such as the metadata service, or Forager's machine with no allow entry listing it.
